Create one high-resolution landscape 3840x2160 design reference sheet: four equally sized photographs in a 2x2 grid, thin white gutters, no captions or labels. All panels show THE SAME physically possible interior, NOT four design alternatives. Image 1 is ONLY a reference for the coherent contemporary Taiwanese home's warm natural palette, photographic realism and level of everyday finish; it is not the room to copy. Create the new room described below. Photographs should resemble an actual lived-in middle-class home, not luxury showroom or CGI. Natural daylight, restrained practical lighting, neutral white balance, physically plausible reflections and contact shadows, nuanced roughness, construction joints, subtle use marks, honest material microtexture. No people, no brands, no text, no diagrams, no impossible joins, no excessive clutter, no plastic shine, no bloom, no exaggerated wide-angle distortion. Maintain the SAME doors, windows, furniture shapes, hardware, and furnishing positions in every view. Use upright verticals and 28-35mm full-frame lenses for wide views, camera about 1.6m high. View details must not invent objects or remodel the room.
ROOM: Entry/hall, 3m wide east-west by 8m long north-south, 3m ceiling. A modest Taiwanese apartment entrance and circulation hall. Solid wood-lined metal front door centered at SOUTH end; five internal room doors: two on WEST at 2m and 6m from south, two matching doors on EAST at 2m and 6m from south, and bathroom door centered at NORTH end. Keep all five internal doorways and main clear walking route legible. A 1.2m long slim light-oak shoe bench and 0.30m deep shoe storage along southeast wall, close to entrance and outside door swings; keys in a shallow tray, one pair of gray house slippers, restrained lived-in traces. Light warm terrazzo entrance strip transitioning to natural oak hall floor, offwhite painted walls with low skirting, a small honest ceiling light rather than dramatic coves, practical utility panel near entrance. No windows inserted in internal corridor walls. TOP LEFT looks north from entrance along hall; TOP RIGHT reverse looks south toward main door; BOTTOM LEFT diagonal view near entrance showing storage depth and clear passage; BOTTOM RIGHT close-up of bench joinery, key tray, shoe and floor transition.

Create one high-resolution 3840x2160 landscape interior-design reference sheet containing four equal photographs in a clean 2x2 grid with very thin white gutters. All four photographs show THE SAME physically possible kitchen/dining room, with identical architecture, appliances, objects and furniture placement. This is an original design reference for building a real-time Blender/Unreal environment.
The room is a modest, lived-in contemporary Taiwanese apartment kitchen/dining room, warm natural materials, plausible ordinary household quality, not a luxury showroom. Interior clear dimensions: 5.0m east-west by 4.0m north-south, ceiling 3.0m. One 1.0m wide doorway centered on WEST wall. One rectangular aluminum-framed daylight window centered on EAST wall, above sink counter. An L-shaped 0.60m deep kitchen run follows EAST and NORTH walls, countertop 0.90m high. Sink below east window. Small two-burner hob on north counter, realistic range hood and backsplash above. A 0.90m wide freestanding brushed-steel side-by-side refrigerator stands at the west end of the north kitchen run; keep its door swing and walkway clear. A compact 1.20m x 0.75m light-oak dining table stands toward SOUTHWEST with two simple chairs, leaving a clear entrance path and at least 1.05m working aisle.
Satin muted sage cabinet fronts, subtle warm-white quartz worktop, 100mm offwhite backsplash tiles with actual fine grout, warm plaster walls, pale low-gloss terrazzo floor. Meaningful human-scale construction details: cabinet door gaps, handles, plinth recess, window reveal thickness, electrical outlets away from water, sink drain and faucet attachments. One unbranded brushed stainless steel cooking pot with TWO black side handles and one offwhite ceramic mug; same design and location in every wide view. Restrained real household details, a folded towel and dish soap near sink, not decorative clutter.
TOP LEFT: eye-height 1.6m view from the west doorway toward northeast, 30mm full-frame lens, verticals upright. TOP RIGHT: reverse view from southeast toward northwest showing the doorway and dining zone. BOTTOM LEFT: view from southwest toward northeast, enough change in perspective to understand counter depth, same layout. BOTTOM RIGHT: close photograph of the sink/counter/cabinet junction showing honest material microtexture and joinery.
Style: indistinguishable from careful real interior photography, natural daylight and restrained 3500K practical lighting, physically credible exposure, soft contact shadows, nuanced roughness, tiny believable wear, brushed steel grain, correct glass reflections, no cinematic color grade, no bloom, no excessive HDR, no plastic CGI sheen, no unrealistically immaculate surfaces. Everything structurally buildable; no floating fixtures, impossible cabinetry, extra doors, duplicated appliances or changing windows. No people, no characters, no brands, no labels, no words, no floor-plan or dimension graphics. Prioritize geometrical consistency and usable modeling detail over decoration.
